h1: The 7 Best AT&T Cordless Phones of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best AT&T Cordless Phones: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven AT&T cordless phones from one-handset basics to five-handset office systems, with call blocking and cell link notes.
summary: The AT&T DL72479 four-handset system is our best overall pick, with smart call blocking and a Bluetooth cell link. The DLP73590 is the home office option with conference calling, the BL108 is the single-base color display model, and the BL102 is the cheapest way into the brand.
intro: AT&T sells a lot of near-identical cordless phones, and the model numbers do little to explain the gap between them. The practical divide is how many handsets you get, whether the call blocker is smart or basic, and whether a Bluetooth link to your mobile is included.

We reviewed eight AT&T systems and kept seven, leaving out a close sibling with the same feature set. The ranking weighs handset count, call blocking type, cell link, display and extras such as conference calling, using spec sheets and owner feedback instead of lab work.

products.name: AT&T DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, 4-Handset, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell, Caller ID Announce, Answering Machine - DL72479
products.verdict: Four handsets, smart blocking and a cell link at a fair bucket.
products.description:
Out of the box the DL72479 gives you four handsets and an answering machine, plus a blocker that screens unknown callers, a Bluetooth link to your mobile and spoken caller names.

It leads because it delivers the strongest feature set at the $50-100 bucket, whereas the BL102-4 offers four handsets with fewer modern extras at a higher bucket. The tradeoff versus the DLP73590 is the screen and conference features.

It suits a family home wanting phones in several rooms. The caveat is that the listing does not mention a color display.
products.idealFor: Families wanting phones in several rooms.

products.name: AT&T 5-Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Home and Business Phone with Answering Machine, 5" Color Display, One-Touch Shortcut, Conference, Intercom, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell - DLP73590
products.verdict: Five handsets, a 5 inch screen and conference calling.
products.description:
The DLP73590 brings five handsets, a 5 inch color display, conference calling, intercom, an answering machine, smart call blocker and Bluetooth Connect to Cell.

It ranks second because it costs more, sitting in the $100-200 bucket, and most households will not use conference calls. For a home office the extras justify it.

It suits remote workers who join calls from a landline. The caveat is the higher spend.
products.idealFor: Home offices that run phone calls.
products.skipIf: You only need basic home use.

products.name: AT&T DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell, Answering Machine, 2.4" Color Display, Big Buttons - BL108
products.verdict: A color screen, big buttons and a cell link in one handset set.
products.description:
The BL108 has a 2.4 inch color display, big buttons, Bluetooth Connect to Cell, a smart call blocker and an answering machine.

It ranks third because it targets a smaller home than the DL72479, though it matches it on key features at the same bucket of $50-100. The handset count is not stated in the listing.

It suits couples in an apartment. The caveat is that you should confirm handsets included.
products.skipIf: You need phones in many rooms.

products.name: AT&T BL102-4 DECT 6.0 4-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Four handsets with audio assist but no Bluetooth link.
products.description:
The BL102-4 provides four handsets, call blocking, an answering machine, a caller ID announcer, audio assist and an intercom.

It ranks fourth because it lacks the cell link of the DL72479 and sits in the $100-200 bucket, a higher spend. Audio assist is its distinguishing feature.

It suits larger landline homes. The caveat is the missing Bluetooth link.
products.skipIf: You want to pair a mobile.

products.name: AT&T TL88102BK DECT 6.0 2-Line Expandable Cordless Phone with Answering System and Dual Caller ID/Call Waiting, 3 Handsets, Black
products.verdict: Handles two phone lines across three handsets.
products.description:
The TL88102BK is a two-line expandable system with three handsets, dual caller ID and call waiting, and an answering system.

It ranks fifth because few buyers actually run two lines, and the price sits in the $200-500 bucket. It is the right choice if you do.

It suits a small business or a home office with two numbers. The caveat is that it is overkill for a single line.

products.name: AT&T EL52113 Cordless Phone with Answering System and Extra-Large Backlit Keys, Light Champagne
products.verdict: Extra-large backlit keys on a single handset.
products.description:
The EL52113 has extra-large backlit keys, an answering system and one handset in a light champagne finish.

It ranks sixth because it has no call blocking or cell link listed. It falls in the $25-50 bucket.

A fit for anyone who struggles with small keys. The caveat is the lack of modern spam protection.
products.idealFor: People who need big dialing keys.

products.name: AT&T BL102 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: The cheapest way into AT&T call blocking and audio assist.
products.description:
The BL102 includes one handset, an answering machine, call blocking, caller ID announcer and audio assist, at the $25-50 bucket.

It ranks last because one handset limits coverage, and there is no cell link. In return you get the call blocking at the lowest price.

It suits a single-room setup. The caveat is that expanding needs extra handsets.

whatMatters.detail: Each handset is a phone you can place in a different room. More handsets raise the price. Count the rooms you actually need and check the number in the title.
Smart call blockers screen unknown numbers automatically, while basic ones just let you block a list. It matters when spam is frequent. Look for smart call blocker in the listing.
This pairs your mobile by Bluetooth so calls ring on the home handsets. It helps where signal is weak indoors. Confirm the phrase in the title.
Most homes have one line, but some offices have two. A two-line system manages both numbers. Check how many lines your provider gives you.
Larger keys and displays help users with poor eyesight. Look for the screen size in inches and descriptors like big or extra-large buttons.

howToChoose.intro: Handset count follows the number of rooms.

cards.label: Smart blocker
cards.text: Filters unknown callers automatically. The DL72479, DLP73590 and BL108 have it.

cards.label: Basic blocking
cards.text: Blocks numbers you add. The BL102 and BL102-4 offer call blocking in basic form.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to a smart blocker if spam is a frequent annoyance.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Conference calling, a large display and a smart call blocker.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The DLP73590 offers all three, while the TL88102BK suits two-line offices.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You work from home and need the DLP73590 conference features.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: A single room is enough, where the BL102 covers the basics.

faq.q: Are AT&T handsets interchangeable between models?
faq.a: Not always. Handsets generally pair with their own base, so check compatibility before mixing.
Most need a phone jack. Some can use Connect to Cell instead.
It boosts volume for hard-to-hear calls. It helps users with mild hearing loss.

faq.q: How do I block a number?
faq.a: Use the call block menu on the handset. Smart blockers also learn from your choices.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Rechargeable batteries decline over years. Replace them with the type in the manual.
Some systems are expandable. Check the number the base supports.

finalTake: The DL72479 is the AT&T we would buy for most homes, with four handsets and the modern call blocking features. Pick the DLP73590 when you work from home, and the BL102 when a single room is enough. Match handset count to rooms before you order.
